title: Retaining Suboptimal Actions to Follow Shifting Optima in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
claim: Existing value-decomposition methods fail to track a shifting optimum, while retaining multiple sub-value functions lets the learner adapt.
layout: 6 panels in 2x3 grid, each an original→shifted matrix pair
description: The figure is a 2x3 grid of panels. Each panel shows a pair of 3x3 payoff or Q-value tables, labeled "Original Value" and "Shifted Value" and joined by a bold arrow. Rows are agent 1's actions A, B and C. Columns are agent 2's actions A, B and C. Panel (a) shows the true payoff of a matrix game, where the optimum moves from (A,A) with value 8 to (C,C) with value 8. Panel (b) shows QMIX's learned Q^tot, which stays stuck on the old optimum. Panel (c) shows WQMIX, which has the same problem. The bottom row shows S2Q with K=2: Q^tot, then sub-value Q1^sub, then Q2^sub. The sub-value tables keep the alternative high-value actions, so the new optimum is recovered. Optimal cells are in bold. The eye goes to the numeric grids and the bold entries.
caption: Fundamental Limitations of value decomposition algorithms. (a): The actual payoff of the matrix game. (b),(c): Training result of QMIX and WQMIX. (d): Training results of S2Q when $K=2$, where $K$ is the hyperparameter controlling number of sub-networks to use.
abstract: Value decomposition is a core approach for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). However, existing methods still rely on a single optimal action and struggle to adapt when the underlying value function shifts during training, often converging to suboptimal policies. To address this limitation, we propose Successive Sub-value Q-learning (S2Q), which learns multiple sub-value functions to retain alternative high-value actions. Incorporating these sub-value functions into a Softmax-based behavior policy, S2Q encourages persistent exploration and enables $Q^{\text{tot}}$ to adjust quickly to the changing optima. Experiments on challenging MARL benchmarks confirm that S2Q consistently outperforms various MARL algorithms, demonstrating improved adaptability and overall performance. Our code is available at https://github.com/hyeon1996/S2Q.
